_comment: Publish-console 'App config' template (deployment defaults, becomes ENCLAVE_CONFIG via configCid). 'volumes' names the attested model volumes the platform attaches (the wasm-manager mounts each at /models/<name> in the guest - no paths here by design). Everything else overlays the config embedded in the wasm, per field, and the 'models' catalog merges per volume key, so a deployment adds or tweaks one model without restating the rest. Attach volumes by the EXACT names the enclave carries; the attach name is the catalog key.
_sizing_comment: SIZING: weights + KV cache at the NODE's context window + ~1.5 GB working set. Maya1 is a dense 3B (28 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128 = ~112 KiB/token at f16 K/V, ~60 KiB at q8_0), and the weights are only 3.5 GB, so the NODE WINDOW is the whole bill: at a 176K q8_0 window the KV term is ~10.7 GB and the deployment wants ~16 GB = gpu 0.12 of a 141 GB H200; f16 K/V nearly doubles that. The app itself never needs a long window (a speaking episode is ~200 prompt tokens + 2048 audio tokens), but llama.cpp allocates the node's full window up front regardless. Do not guess from these numbers: GET /health computes them from the node's own environment and reports `fits` per model with the shortfall spelled out, and the app REFUSES a model it cannot serve rather than attempting it (a CUDA OOM inside compute() aborts the whole tenant).
_auth_comment: SET AN API KEY. api_key gates the /v1/* surface (the OpenAI-compatible endpoint); the playground routes - including /speak, which is the page's engine - stay open, same posture as the sibling GPU apps: an app-level password on a public page protects nothing an attacker wants, and a PRIVATE deployment is the fleet's real gate for the data path. Reference the credential as a SECRET BY NAME as below, never the literal: this file is published on-chain by CID and world-readable. Set the value in the deployment's secrets ({"set":{"SPEECH_GENERATOR_API_KEY":"<key>"}}) and restart.
_speech_comment: A SPEECH VOLUME is an ordinary ggml volume plus snac_decoder.bin (the guest-side audio codec; fetch-model.sh derives it deterministically and pins its sha256). A volume missing that file is listed by /health with why_mute rather than served silently wrong. The host needs NO audio support of any kind - the model is an ordinary Llama to it - so any node that serves eyesoff-ai serves this. GET /health?probe=1 checks both halves: a real session open (GPU) and a real parse of the volume's SNAC decoder (CPU).
